question: What is context engineering, and how is it different from prompt engineering?
idealAnswerCore: Prompt engineering is the wording of instructions; context engineering is the system that decides what tokens enter the window each turn — retrieved docs, tool results, memories, history, schemas — under token, cache, and freshness constraints.
idealAnswerFraming: This is the 2025–2026 name for what production teams actually do. Interviewers want a pipeline, not a prettier system prompt.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Inputs: user message, system policy, RAG, tools, memory, structured state
Budgets: reserve tokens for output, tools, and a stable prefix for caching
Quality: too little context → hallucination; too much → lost-in-the-middle and cost
Version the assembler like code; eval it like a retriever
Prompt copy is one module inside the assembler, not the whole job

question: What should always live in the stable prompt prefix versus the per-turn suffix?
idealAnswerCore: Put immutable policy, tool schemas, and static style rules in a byte-stable prefix so provider prompt caches hit; put user text, retrieved chunks, and timestamps in the suffix so they do not bust the cache or leak across users.
idealAnswerFraming: Tie to Anthropic/OpenAI prefix caching. Give a layout.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Prefix: system policy, tool JSON schemas, static few-shots
Suffix: user query, RAG hits, conversation tail
Never put another tenant's data or the current date in the cached prefix
Changing one character of the prefix invalidates the cache for everyone
Measure cache hit rate after every prompt edit

question: How do you compact a long conversation without losing constraints the user stated?
idealAnswerCore: Keep the last N turns verbatim, maintain a structured state object for durable constraints (name, IDs, 'never email the customer'), and summarize the rest with an explicit 'do not drop constraints' prompt — then eval compaction on a golden set of constraint-carry tests.
idealAnswerFraming: This is the production memory problem. Structured state beats a fuzzy paragraph summary.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Extract slots: goals, entities, bans, pending tool results
Verbatim tail preserves tone and recent corrections
Tell the user when history was compacted
Never compact away safety or billing constraints
Test: 'always reply in French' still holds after 40 turns

question: How should tool results be placed in context so they stay useful and safe?
idealAnswerCore: Treat tool output as untrusted data in a delimited block, truncate or schema-project huge payloads, keep a handle to the full blob in your store, and never let a 200k log dump crowd out the user question.
idealAnswerFraming: Agents die from stuffing curl output into the window. Show truncation + pointer pattern.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Project: keep fields the model needs (id, status, error), drop blobs
Hash or URL to fetch more via another tool if required
Delimit as data, not as new system instructions
Cap per-tool tokens; summarize tables
Eval: can the agent still answer after a verbose tool?

question: When do you use long context, RAG, or external memory for the same product question?
idealAnswerCore: Long context for one or few documents the user just uploaded; RAG for a large, changing corpus with citations; external memory for durable user/state facts — most products use all three with a router, not one slogan.
idealAnswerFraming: Classic design fork. Give failure modes of each.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Long context: simple, loses middle, expensive, weak ACLs at chunk level
RAG: scalable, needs chunking/eval, can miss if retrieval fails
Memory: preferences and tickets, not the knowledge base
Do not embed the entire chat into the vector store by default
Measure $ and faithfulness for each path

question: What is context rot (or lost-in-the-middle), and how do you design around it?
idealAnswerCore: Models use the start and end of a long prompt better than the middle; stuffing more chunks can lower accuracy. Put the question and the best evidence at the edges, rerank aggressively, and keep k small.
idealAnswerFraming: Cite the lost-in-the-middle result. Product implication: bigger window ≠ better.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Rerank to 5–10 chunks instead of 50
Repeat the user question after documents
Break multi-hop into sub-questions instead of one giant pack
Eval with needles at different positions
Long-context models still show U-shaped use; measure, do not assume

question: How do you assemble context for a coding agent over a large repository?
idealAnswerCore: Do not dump the repo: retrieve by semantic + grep + dependency graph, pin open files and the patch hunk, keep a map of paths, and use tools to read more — the window holds a working set, not the monorepo.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Always include: user instruction, current file/selection, compiler errors
Retrieve: similar code, definitions, tests for the symbol
Ignore generated lockfiles and node_modules
Budget: code is token-heavy; prefer snippets with line numbers
Eval on SWE-like tasks plus your private repo golden patches

question: How do you keep context packing deterministic enough for evals and prompt cache, but personalized per user?
idealAnswerCore: Split the pack into a global immutable prefix, a tenant-stable middle (tools allowed for this plan), and a request-specific tail; hash each layer; evals freeze retrieval snapshots so you are not scoring a moving index.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Record prompt_hash, retrieval_ids, memory_ids on every trace
Golden evals pin chunk IDs, not live search
Personalization belongs in the tail or a small cached-per-user segment
Feature flags that change tools must version the prefix
Flaky packing is an eval flake — sort chunks by id if scores tie

question: How do you count tokens for context budgets, and why do naive character estimates fail?
idealAnswerCore: Use the same tokenizer as the target model (or the provider's count API); character/4 heuristics fail on code, CJK, and special tokens, and you must reserve max_output plus tool schemas or you will overflow at runtime.
idealAnswerFraming: Practical. Mention different tokenizers per model in a multi-provider gateway.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Count system + tools + history + RAG + user before calling
Reserve output tokens or the API truncates JSON
Images/audio have their own token tariffs
A gateway that routes GPT vs Claude cannot share one counter
Fail with a user-visible 'too long' and a compact action, not a raw 400

question: What is a context assembler (or prompt compiler), and why put it in one module?
idealAnswerCore: A single assembler function owns ordering, budgets, redaction, and hashes so product features cannot each concatenate strings into the prompt — that is how injection, cache misses, and irreproducible bugs happen.
idealAnswerFraming: Software architecture for LLM apps. One choke point.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: API: structured parts in, ChatMessage[] out
Enforces delimiters and privilege (system vs data)
Applies DLP/redaction before send
Unit-testable with fixtures
The rest of the app never string-concats a prompt

question: How do you handle conflicting context (old memory vs new doc vs user correction)?
idealAnswerCore: Define a precedence policy: explicit user correction > current-turn retrieved source with recency > long-term memory > model priors; show conflicts when stakes are high instead of silently averaging.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Stamp memories with time and source

question: How does context packing change for reasoning models with large hidden thoughts?
idealAnswerCore: Leave headroom for reasoning tokens, keep evidence tight so thoughts are not crowding RAG, and do not automatically append previous thoughts into the next pack — they are expensive, sometimes sensitive, and usually redundant with the final answer.
idealAnswerFraming: Connect the two new domains. Budget is shared.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: max_output includes thoughts on some APIs — read the docs

question: Why is 'just put everything in the prompt' a bad context strategy even with huge windows?
idealAnswerCore: Huge windows still cost, still miss the middle, still mix untrusted data with instructions, and still weaken caching and ACLs — retrieval and packing remain the control plane.
idealAnswerFraming: Push back on the 'RAG is dead' take without being dogmatic.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Cost scales with input tokens every call
Attention is uneven across positions
Tenants and secrets should not all sit in one blob
Prompt cache wants stability, not a unique 800k dump
Ops: you cannot debug what you cannot name (chunk IDs)

question: How would you design context for a multi-agent system so agents do not leak or duplicate state?
idealAnswerCore: Give each agent the minimum working set plus a shared structured blackboard (task graph, artifacts, IDs); do not paste the full orchestrator transcript into every worker; pass handles to files in object storage instead of inlined blobs.
idealAnswerFraming: Multi-agent context is a distributed-systems problem.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Per-agent system prompts stay specialized and cacheable
Shared store: tickets, patches, retrieval IDs
Summarize worker output before sending to the parent
ACL: a research agent should not see payroll tools in its schema
Trace the blackboard, not only the chat

question: How do you redact PII in context without breaking the model's ability to complete the task?
idealAnswerCore: Replace secrets with stable placeholders (CUSTOMER_1, TOKEN_A) that you map back after generation, keep format (email-shaped) if the task needs it, and never embed raw PAN/keys in RAG or traces — test that the model still joins entities correctly.
idealAnswerKeyPoints: Deterministic placeholders so 'Alice' stays the same across chunks
Do not hash in a way that breaks referential mentions
Rehydrate only in the UI for authorized users
Some tasks (fraud) need real values inside a tighter ACL path
Eval entity resolution after redaction
